newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of broad EMU recover - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of broad EMU recover - JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad-based European monetary union, including Italy, Spain and Sweden, steadied after three weeks of decline and edged higher over the past week, according to JP Morgan's EMU calculator.
In the past five trading days, market prices indicated that the perceived probabilities of Spain, Sweden, Italy, Denmark and the UK joining Germany in EMU in 1999 all increased.
The perceived probability of Italy taking part rose 3.0 percentage points to 64 percent and Spain rose 2.0 points to 66 percent. Sweden rose 1.0 point to 65 percent.
Over the month, however, EMU expectations are still down a net 10.0 points in Italy, down 13.0 points in Spain and down 8.0 in Sweden.
Elsewhere, the perceived probability of the UK joining EMU in 1999 rose 6.0 points over the week but remains low overall with an estimated 38 percent chance. Denmark rose 10 points to 45 percent.
The market still believes there is a 100 percent chance of France and Belgium joining in 1999, which was the same as last week, the calculator showed.
JP Morgan's EMU calculator is derived from the interest rate swaps market.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
